Subject: Re: Proposal: Regional Escalation Slabs + Trial On-call Addendum

Alice — thanks. Short answers up front: yes, we can do a 60–90 day pilot that includes a capped on-call addendum, and we have a modular regional-failover credit that scales by uptime exposure and request burn-rate. Details below plus a draft term sheet attached.

Summary of options (high level):
- Regional Failover Credit: when a failover is triggered and traffic routes to the secondary region, we apply a percentage credit to the monthly invoice based on the measured token-seconds served from the failover region and the duration of the outage. The credit scale is 15% for partial degradation (reduced throughput), 35% for full failover under 12 hours, and 55% for full failover beyond 12 hours.

- Escalation Slabs (response / coverage):
  * Bronze: 24x7 email + next-business-hour triage (included)
  * Silver: 8x5 phone + 2 hour critical response window (add-on)
  * Gold: 24x7 on-call + 30-minute critical response (retainer/commit)

- Pilot on-call addendum proposal: 30 hours of on-call for the pilot window (60 days) billed as a fixed refundable retainer of $6,000. If you convert to a 12-month Gold retainer within 30 days post-pilot, we credit 50% of the retainer against first three months of the contract.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Credits are metered by our token throughput logs (we can provide a sample CSV showing token-second buckets). Credits apply only to hosted capacity and exclude committed Dedicated pool charges unless you opt into cross-region commit.
- The pilot on-call hours are scheduled and triaged through our Console; we require a 48-hour advance window for any non-urgent scheduled work to avoid conflicting with production rotations.

Attachments: SLA_TermSheet_BG_v1.pdf (term sheet with tables), Pilot_Oncall_SOW.docx (scope + scheduling template).

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached the term sheet. Can you share this with procurement and tell us the key redlines (if any) to prioritize?
2) Jordan will scope pricing options based on an expected monthly token volume — copying him in.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: Regional Escalation Slabs + Trial On-call Addendum

Alice — I ran some numbers against the volumes you shared during the demo. Two priceable paths we recommend so you can choose the commitment-risk profile:

Option A — Pilot-first (low commitment):
- 60-day pilot with 30 on-call hours (refundable retainer $6k).
- Post-pilot: standard hosted rates + option to buy Gold retainer at $18k/mo (24x7 on-call) with a 12-month minimum. No upfront volume commit required.
- Regional failover: credits applied as Camila outlined (15/35/55). No discount on pricing unless you convert to a 12-month retainer within 30 days.

Option B — Commit-first (discounted):
- 12-month commit that includes 24x7 Gold retainer for $12.5k/mo (15% list discount vs A).
- Includes a built-in regional-failover buffer: first 48 hours of failover covered with no crediting required (useful for short incidents).
- Quarterly true-up for token usage; overages billed at a blended committed rate.

A few clarifying operational points:
- The refundable retainer flows to a credit ledger. If BrightGrid converts, it appears as credit on the first invoice. If not, we refund 70% (to cover scheduling frictions).
- For billing simplicity we can surface a single line item for "Premium Response (Gold)" and separate "Regional Failover Buffer" as a meter.

Kimberly, a quick ask: are there any constraints from an ops/roster perspective that would prevent us from committing the 30 pilot hours within a typical two-week rotation window?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Camila / Alice — operationally this looks fine. A couple of practical notes that matter for SOW and procurement redlines: 

1) Scheduling: We can commit the 30 pilot hours within 60 days; we’ll lock up-to-3 recurring 4-hr blocks per week so coverage is predictable. We require a single BrightGrid escalation contact and an on-call runbook link prior to the pilot start.

2) Measured credits: credits are calculated against per-minute token-second aggregates. For the pilot, we’ll supply a CSV sample and a short runbook on how we compute the credit so procurement can validate.

3) Audit & evidence: for larger credits (>35%) we require incident postmortem and evidence of failover routes (CloudFront/Load Balancer logs are fine). Procurement often asks for that up front — if you want, include a placeholder acceptance clause in the term sheet.

4) DocuSign: I made two minor non-substantive edits to the attached term sheet (section numbering + typo). Camila — please reattach and I’ll route to Legal for a quick look.

Alice — if that aligns, we can turn this into a DocuSign pilot SOW and schedule kickoff the week of Oct 6.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
